passage: It was a Wednesday, after the last bell, when Binita told me she had not eaten since the morning and that she was afraid to go home some evenings. I'm Tenzin, and I've gone over that afternoon many times. She made me promise to tell no one, and I said okay, because I wanted her to keep trusting me. Then for days I carried it alone, watching her push her lunch away and flinch when a phone rang. I couldn't sleep. In the end I decided that a promise doesn't mean much if she's hurt. I told her first: "I'm going to tell the counsellor, and I'll be with you." She was angry, then she cried. We went together.

qa.q: On which day did Binita tell Tenzin she was afraid to go home?
qa.a: On a Wednesday, after the last bell.

qa.q: Why did Tenzin tell the counsellor even though Binita had asked for secrecy?
qa.a: Tenzin was afraid Binita was in real danger and realised a promise doesn't mean much if she's hurt. Carrying it alone kept Tenzin awake.

qa.q: What did Tenzin do well in how the secret was broken?
qa.a: Tenzin told Binita first what would happen, and offered to go with her, so it did not feel like a betrayal behind her back. 🤍

qa.q: How might Binita have felt when Tenzin said the counsellor would be told?
qa.a: Angry at first, perhaps scared of what would happen, and then she cried, which may show relief that someone was taking her situation seriously.

grounding: The protagonist fears a friend is in danger and tells a trusted adult, telling the friend first, instead of carrying it alone.

passage:
Monday, 8 pm

I did it today. I told.

For two weeks Deepak has been giving away his tiffin. His shirt has been the same since last Wednesday. Today in PT he nearly fell over during the warm-up. At break he finally admitted his mother has been in hospital in Nagpur for three weeks and his father went with her, and he's alone at home with nobody cooking. He made me promise not to tell.

I couldn't keep that one. At the end of break I said, "Deepak, I'm going to tell Kulkarni Sir. Not to get you in trouble. Because you're not okay and I can't fix this." He was angry. He called me a traitor.

I went straight to the staffroom. Sir listened, then called Deepak's uncle in Wardha from the office phone while I was still there. The uncle is coming tonight. Sir also sent Deepak to the canteen with a lunch pass.

He's still angry with me. I think I'd do it again.

Jatin

qa.q: Where has Deepak's mother been for three weeks?
qa.a: Deepak's mother has been in hospital in Nagpur for three weeks.

qa.q: What was Jatin feeling after telling Kulkarni Sir?
qa.a: Jatin felt worried and hurt by Deepak's anger but also sure that telling was right, saying the choice would be the same again.

qa.q: Why was it wise for Jatin to speak to Deepak before going to the staffroom?
qa.a: Jatin told Deepak directly about going to Kulkarni Sir and why, instead of breaking the promise behind his back.

qa.q: How might Deepak see Jatin's choice in a few weeks?
qa.a: Deepak may still feel embarrassed, but once his uncle is there and he is eating properly, he may see that Jatin was looking after him.

grounding: It shows a teen who fears a friend is in real danger from neglect at home, breaks the secret to a trusted adult out of care, tells the friend, and the teacher acts that day.

passage:
Irawati: r u awake
Disha: ya what happened
Irawati: papa is drunk again. he threw a plate at the wall. mummy is crying
Irawati: i locked my door
Disha: are u hurt??
Irawati: no. just scared. dont tell anyone pls. it will make it worse
Disha: Ira i'm really glad u told me
Disha: but i can't keep this one. i'm going to tell my mum right now. i'm telling u first so u know
Irawati: disha no
Disha: u matter more than the secret. stay in ur room with the door locked. keep ur phone with u
Irawati: ok

Disha ran to the living room. Her mother read the messages, called the child helpline, then called Irawati's Masi, who lives two streets away.

Disha: masi is coming to get u. she'll knock and say it's her
Disha: my mum is on the phone with the helpline people too
Irawati: ok. thank u. i'm still scared
Disha: i know. i'm staying up with u till she's there

qa.q: Who did Disha's mother call after reading the messages?
qa.a: Disha's mother called the child helpline, then called Irawati's Masi.

qa.q: What was Disha feeling when she decided to tell her mum?
qa.a: Disha felt frightened for Irawati's safety and protective, and was willing to face Irawati's anger to keep her safe.

qa.q: Why was it wise for Disha to tell Irawati before telling her mum?
qa.a: It kept trust honest, since Irawati knew what was happening and why, even though she did not want it.

qa.q: What is it like for Irawati to hear that Masi is coming?
qa.a: Irawati is still scared, but may also feel relieved and less alone, knowing a trusted adult is on the way that same night.

grounding: It shows a teen who fears a friend is in danger at home, tells the friend she is breaking the secret, and gets a trusted adult to act that same night.
